title: Three Terms and One Short Tube
subtitle: 能源利用 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 能源利用（环境保护·能源与可再生）
meta: 主题语境：能源利用（环境保护·能源与可再生）　|　核心词汇：steam　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 steam 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1984 the researcher ① saw the steam that no student in the lab would have counted, and he said the seeing was the whole of the term. The ② steam, meaning the vapour itself and not the tube, ran three terms and stayed uncounted in the book; steam, he said, is the only thing in a lab that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ sample of steam in that lab had the same short tube beside it, and the ④ steam at the far bench, meaning the sample they kept for the children to test and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Steam, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the researcher said the counting is the part that fills three terms.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the steam was the whole of the matter, meaning the power and not the vapour. The ⑥ steam, meaning the power and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; steam, he said, is either something you see or the only word that means both vapour and a power. He said the power is the part they remember.

By 1989 the ⑦ steam had become a line in a paper, and the paper had become an argument about the short tube. The ⑧ steam of the whole thing, the researcher wrote in February, was one lab and three terms of counting; steam, he said, is either the sample at the far bench or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ steam I remember is the steam counted in the paper, which closed in 1991 and is still counted as the quietest in the lab. ⑩ Steam, my mother said in 1993, is the only thing that improves by being counted; all steam, she said, is a power that has agreed to look like vapour. She said the power was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 蒸汽（指实验室里每一份旁边的那一份）
B. n. 蒸汽（指那股蒸汽本身，与细细的试管相对）
C. 固定搭配：see the steam 看见这一股蒸汽
D. n. 蒸汽（指留给孩子们测的那一份）
E. n. 蒸汽之事（抽象总称，指一处实验室的蒸汽之事）
F. n. 蒸汽（指研究报告里写到、被清点的那一股）
G. n. 蒸汽、力道（指一件事里人人都测却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 力道（抽象总称，指人人都测却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: saw the steam that no student in the lab would have counted
The steam, meaning the vapour itself and not the tube
Every sample of steam in that lab
the steam at the far bench
the steam was the whole of the matter
the steam had become a line in a paper
The steam of the whole thing

answers.why: see the steam 意为“看见这一股蒸汽”，1984 年那位研究员把实验室里没有一位学生肯清点的一股蒸汽做了一遍。
steam 意为“蒸汽”，指那股蒸汽本身而不是细细的试管，它经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被清点。
steam 意为“蒸汽”，指实验室里每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一支细细的试管。
steam 意为“蒸汽”，指最远那张实验台的留给孩子们测的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
steam 意为“蒸汽、力道”，指一件事里人人都测却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这股力道就是那件事的全部。
steam 意为“力道”，指人人都测却无人提起的那样东西而不是那股蒸汽，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
steam 意为“蒸汽”，指研究报告里写到、被清点的那一股，到 1989 年这一股成了研究报告里的一行。
steam 意为“蒸汽之事”，研究员二月写道，整件事的蒸汽之事是一处实验室和三个学期的清点。
steam 意为“蒸汽”，我记得的是研究报告里清点过的那一股，1991 年测定了，至今仍被说成实验室里最安静的一股。
steam 为抽象总称，母亲 1993 年说，蒸汽是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的蒸汽。
